newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Ballast Nedam to increase European focus.
newsitem.headline: Ballast Nedam to increase European focus.

text.p: Dutch builder Ballast Nedam said on Friday it would continue to shift the focus of its operations to Europe to reduce its risk profile.

"We will continue to shift from Construction International into Construction Europe to reduce risks, while at the same time maintaining international turnover at current levels," Ballast chairman Werner Ludwig told a news conference.
The firm on Thursday reported net profit down fractionally at 91.5 million guilders ($48 million) from a year-earlier 92.1 million.
Ballast's Construction Europe division generated 52 percent of group turnover last year, up from 47 percent in 1995.
"This has given Ballast a more stable base, although Europe is a market with narrower margins," finance director Geert Wirken said.
He said net margins had narrowed to 2.4 percent in 1996 from four percent in 1992, when the construction group's Middle Eastern exposure amounted to some 36 percent of turnover.

Ludwig said he expected the Saudi Arabian market to continue generating annual turnover of around 500-600 million guilders, roughly in line with 1996 but well down on earlier peaks of one billion guilders.
"We plan to maintain current turnover levels at the Construction International division and ensure good profitability," Ludwig said.
The company would also seek to maintain its current share of the dredging market, where margins were seen improving on the back of increased volumes, Ludwig said.
